targets.production_path: onSubmitClick — the security-critical anonymous-bypass gate (line 282): `val anonymousAllowed = provider?.supportsAnonymous == true && state.anonymousMode`. Phase 1.5 (2026-05-04, operator's 6th anti-bluff invocation) added the `supportsAnonymous` conjunct: the global Anonymous-Access toggle MUST only take effect for providers that DECLARE supportsAnonymous=true. Without it, toggling Anonymous on then picking a no-anonymous tracker (RuTracker CAPTCHA_LOGIN, Kinozal/NNM-Club FORM_LOGIN) silently bypasses the credentials check and signals the Search tab as Authorized with NO real authentication — the canonical §6.G/§6.J 'tests green, feature broken/insecure for users' failure.

targets.mutation: Replaced `val anonymousAllowed = provider?.supportsAnonymous == true && state.anonymousMode` with `val anonymousAllowed = state.anonymousMode` (line 282) — i.e. reverted the Phase 1.5 gate so the anonymous bypass fires for ANY provider whose global toggle is on, regardless of capability. Non-crashing: login 'succeeds' (it just succeeds insecurely for a provider that should require credentials).

targets.discrimination: Localized: 1-of-13 failed. With the gate dropped, a FORM_LOGIN/supportsAnonymous=false provider takes the anonymous-bypass short-circuit and emits LoginSideEffect.Success (and would call authService.signalAuthorized, unblocking the Search tab for an un-authenticated provider). The test expected the real auth round-trip to proceed (a State emission) and instead saw SideEffectItem(value=Success) — the security-bypass signal. The other 12 ViewModel tests stayed GREEN. PRIMARY assertions are on user-visible/security-equivalent state (Success side effect NOT emitted, signalAuthorized NOT called, creds NOT marked Invalid), per §6.J clause 3.
